subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Fiberglass: The Everyday Composite
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fiberglass: The Everyday Composite.

hook.text: Your bathtub, boat hull, and car bumper probably share the same material: fiberglass.

buildup.text: Fiberglass weaves thin glass strands into a fabric, then sets it in polyester or epoxy resin.

discovery.text: Glass is brittle alone. But as thin fibers in resin, it becomes flexible, strong, and corrosion-resistant.

twist.text: Fiberglass was discovered in 1932 when a researcher aimed compressed air at molten glass and got fine threads.

climax.text: Wind turbine blades up to 100 meters long are fiberglass. The material that started in bathtubs now harvests energy.

punchline.text: Spin glass into thread. Wrap it in resin. Build anything.

quiz.question: How was fiberglass accidentally discovered?
options: Molten glass was dropped into water and formed threads
Compressed air aimed at molten glass produced fine strands
A factory explosion scattered glass into fiber-like shapes
